newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - trade.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Wednesday were seen mostly steady with a firm tone, amid expectations for light hog marketings, livestock dealers said.

Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered to the plant could range from $58.00 to $59.00 per cwt and Illinois top prices could match Tuesday's of $58.00 at the plant, the dealers said.
Indiana/Ohio top hog prices at the plant could range from $56.00 to $57.50, they said.
Marketings were expected to be light as harvesting momentum builds in the western Corn Belt.

Cash hog prices also were expected to be supported by stronger packer demand as plants look to replenish inventories. Packers reportedly on Tuesday used some the hog inventories gathered Monday that was not used because of light slaughter schedules that day, market sources said.
Outlooks for steady to higher pork prices later Tuesday also generated ideas that hog demand would be strong. Pork prices were seen lifted by Monday's light production.
At midday, fresh loins were quoted by USDA $1.00 per cwt higher and hams steady in a narrow test, but bellies were generally $2.00 lower.
